newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai Ind hits record before retreating.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Ind hits record before retreating.

text.p: Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd shares hit an all-time high of HK$36.20 in early trade on Thursday before profit-taking moved in to reverse the rising trend, brokers said.
The shares retreated to HK$34.60, down HK$0.90, after rising HK$0.70 to HK$36.20.
"The latest rally is based on expectations of asset injections and the report of good 1996 earnings later today," said Jason Tang, a broker of South China Brokerage.
"But light profit taking set in as people believed the recent sharp price rise is a bit of an overreaction (to these expectations)," he added.
Shares of the Shanghai city government controlled company jumped HK$2.40, or 7.25 percent, to HK$35.50 on Wednesday.
Analysts said the market expected the company to announce an asset injection plan or the company's business development plan following its annual results announcement due later on Thursday.
The asset-injection concept has driven the stock more than 380 pecent above its IPO price of HK$7.28 per share in nine-months time.
